elements.text: Completed a basic log implementation with the following:
log reference injected alongside config, through construct of p2p or full_node:p2p or server::full_node::p2p and then all other objects that require logging.
class tracker (base class to log object refcounts) accepts log object and logs checked (debug) builds.
logger posts each message to its own strand on its own low priority threadpool.
logger exposes standard subscriber for accepting log messages.
log handler in bn.exe subscribes to log and emits messages to console.
message notifications preserve order and with handlers invoked non-concurrently.
logger can be easily expanded to differentiate category and parameterization, either with multiple subscribers or via filtering within a subscriber.
Macro invocation both preserves serialization formatting and allows full exclusion at compile time.

text:
Completed a basic log implementation with the following:
• log reference injected alongside config, through construct of p2p or full_node:p2p or server::full_node::p2p and then all other objects that require logging.
• class tracker (base class to log object refcounts) accepts log object and logs checked (debug) builds.
• logger posts each message to its own strand on its own low priority threadpool.
• logger exposes standard subscriber for accepting log messages.
• log handler in bn.exe subscribes to log and emits messages to console.
• message notifications preserve order and with handlers invoked non-concurrently.
• logger can be easily expanded to differentiate category and parameterization, either with multiple subscribers or via filtering within a subscriber.
• Macro invocation both preserves serialization formatting and allows full exclusion at compile time.

        << static_cast<uint16_t>(reject->code) << ") from [" << authority()
        << "] with reason: " << reject->reason);```

elements.text: Preserving serial formatting while also posting discrete messages requires construction of a closure for each write, which is an additional cost that is excluded when messages are compiled out. Each message is serialized to a stringstring, which is then flushed to post. But the posted messages are then captured by subscription handlers, and these can queue up writes to the log output (such as the console or file) without flushing them on each write. This is a material performance improvement.

Each message is serialized to a stringstring, which is then flushed to post. But the posted messages are then captured by subscription handlers, and these can queue up writes to the log output (such as the console or file) without flushing them on each write. This is a material performance improvement.

elements.text: This worked out nicely, tested and merged. I've added a bn command line option that disables console out. This dramatically reduces shutdown latency with high volume logging. I'm now testing at 5,000 connections, batched 5 at a time (25,000 connection attempts). These levels of connectivity used to crash my router. The new one has had no problems. CPU is almost nothing (~.15%), memory is a modest linear scale, and I/O is also small. I've got 32 of my 64 cores configured on network, but it's never using more than 10. Still not a single crash or deadlock and shutdown is almost instantaneous regardless of the connection count.
